userMessages.text:
# Reliable webhook delivery

We are building a multi-tenant webhook delivery subsystem. Product services publish webhook events through an internal ingress API, and the ingress transaction must durably record each accepted event before acknowledging it. A dispatcher expands the event into one delivery per subscribed endpoint and puts those deliveries on a durable queue. Delivery workers load the tenant's active signing secret, sign the exact payload, and call the customer endpoint with an idempotency key.

A 2xx response completes the delivery. Timeouts, network failures, and retryable responses return through a retry scheduler using exponential backoff with jitter and a maximum attempt count. Permanent failures and exhausted retries go to a dead-letter queue with the payload, endpoint, attempt history, and last error intact. Operators can inspect and replay dead-lettered deliveries without changing their original event identity. Endpoint configuration can be paused, and paused endpoints retain deliveries until they are resumed. Delivery attempts and outcomes feed tenant-visible status history and operational metrics.
